questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
The owner of an unoccupied duplex needed to paint its interior in preparation for renting each unit. Before leaving the country on a three-month-long business trip, the owner offered a painter $3,000 to paint the interior of each unit of the duplex. The painter told the owner that he would try to fit the job into his busy schedule. The owner replied that she would be out of the country for three months but would leave the key to each unit under the front doormat. There was no further communication between them.
Ten weeks later the painter began to paint one of the duplex units. Concerned that she had heard nothing from the painter about completing the task, the owner emailed a friend asking him to paint the duplex for $3,000. The friend sent an email accepting the owner's offer and began painting the other duplex unit the following day.
Is the painter likely to prevail in a breach of contract action against the owner?

choices.A: No, because an offeree must notify an offeror that performance has begun in order to create a contractual obligation between them.
choices.B: No, because notification is required to enforce a contractual duty when the offeror has no convenient way of ascertaining if performance has begun.
choices.C: Yes, because an offeree may always accept an offer by making a return promise or by beginning performance.
choices.D: Yes, because notification that an offeree has begun to perform is only required if the offeror explicitly requested notification.

questions.explanation:
An offer to form a bilateral contract—ie, an offer that invites acceptance by return promise—can be expressly accepted with a return promise or impliedly accepted by starting performance.* Notice is not required to accept an offer by starting performance unless the offer so requires (Choice A). However, if the offeree should know that the offeror has no convenient way of learning within a reasonable time that performance has begun, the offeree must notify the offeror. Failure to do so will discharge the offeror's contractual duty (Choice D).

Here, the duplex owner offered the painter $3,000 to paint the interior of each unit. Although the painter made no return promise (he would "try to fit the job into his schedule"), he began to paint the duplex 10 weeks later (acceptance by starting performance). The painter knew that the owner was out of the country (no convenient way to learn about performance), so he had to notify her that performance had begun. Since he did not, the owner's contractual duty was discharged, and the painter is not likely to prevail in his breach-of-contract action.

*Acceptance is also implied when the offeree accepts a valuable benefit (eg, money, property, services) by conduct or failure to act. This method of acceptance is not available here because the valuable benefit ($3,000 payment) could not be accepted until performance was completed.

(Choice C) The assertion that an offeree can always accept an offer by making a return promise or by beginning performance is overbroad. The offeror, as master of the offer, can dictate the manner or means of acceptance.

📌 Educational Objective

Notice is not required to effectively accept an offer by starting performance unless the offer so requires. But if the offeree should know that the offeror has no convenient way of learning within a reasonable time that performance has begun, the offeree must notify the offeror. Otherwise, the offeror's contractual duty will be discharged.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 62 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (effect of performance by offeree where offer invites either performance or promise).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 54 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (acceptance by performance and necessity of notification to offeror).
questions.zh-question:
一栋空置双拼屋的业主需要粉刷其内部，为出租每个单元做准备。在出国进行为期三个月的商务旅行之前，该业主向一名油漆工发出要约，愿意支付3000美元，请其粉刷该双拼屋每个单元的内部。油漆工告诉业主，他会尽力将这项工作安排到他繁忙的日程中。业主回复说，她将出国三个月，但会把每个单元的钥匙留在前门门垫下。此后他们之间没有进一步的沟通。

十周后，油漆工开始粉刷其中一个双拼屋单元。由于未收到油漆工关于完成任务的任何消息，业主感到担忧，便通过电子邮件联系了一位朋友，请他以3000美元的价格粉刷该双拼屋。该朋友回信接受了业主的要约，并于次日开始粉刷另一个双拼屋单元。

油漆工对业主提起的违约诉讼是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为受要约人必须通知要约人其已开始履行，才能在双方之间建立合同义务。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为当要约人没有便捷方式确定履行是否已经开始时，为强制执行合同义务，通知是必需的。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为受要约人总可以通过作出对待承诺或开始履行来接受要约。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为只有在要约人明确要求通知的情况下，才需要受要约人就其已开始履行进行通知。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Acceptance by Performance & Notice
⚖️ 核心法律规则 (The Rule) 根据《合同法重述（第二次）》§ 54 (Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 54)：

虽然受要约人 (Offeree) 可以通过开始履行 (Beginning Performance) 来接受要约，通常无需通知。但是，如果受要约人有理由知道要约人 (Offeror) 无法在合理时间内便捷地得知履行已经开始，受要约人必须履行通知义务。

若未通知，要约人的合同义务将被免除 (Discharged)。

🔍 案情逻辑分析

1. 要约 (Offer)：
业主提供 $3,000 请求粉刷房屋。这是一个寻求行为作为承诺的要约。

2. 接受 (Acceptance)：
油漆工最初说“尽力安排”（这只是模棱两可的陈述，非承诺）。但在10周后，他开始粉刷。根据法律，开始履行即构成接受，合同在此时形式上成立。

3. 关键障碍 (The Issue)：
业主在国外，且没有便捷途径知晓。
油漆工明知业主出国3个月，且双方无沟通。这意味着业主无法自动得知“履行已开始”。

4. 后果 (Consequence)：
由于油漆工未尽到通知义务 (Duty to Notify)，业主的付款义务被免除。因此，业主雇佣朋友的行为不构成违约。

✅ 正确答案：选项 B

"No, because notification is required to enforce a contractual duty when the offeror has no convenient way of ascertaining if performance has begun."

解析：这个选项精准地描述了本案的例外情况。虽然通常“开始履行”就是接受，但在要约人无法知情的情况下，为了强制执行 (Enforce) 对方的付款义务，受要约人必须发出通知。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？

选项 A (错误)： 虽然结论是No，但理由错误。法律原则上不要求必须通知才能“建立”合同义务（Acceptance by performance通常无需通知）。本案是因为特殊情况（业主无法知情）才导致义务被免除。
选项 C (错误)： "Always"（总是）过于绝对。要约人是要约的主人 (Master of the Offer)，可以规定必须通过某种方式接受。此外，该选项忽略了本题考查的“通知义务免除责任”这一考点。
选项 D (错误)： 错误地认为只有在“明确要求”时才需通知。根据 Restatement § 54(2)，即使未明确要求，如果受要约人知道要约人无法得知履行情况，也必须通知。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 遇到 Acceptance by Performance（通过履行接受）的题目时，请按以下步骤思考：
  1. 是否开始履行了？(是 = 合同成立)
  2. 要约人能看到或知道吗？
  3. 如果不能（如本题中的出国、远距离），受要约人通知了吗？
  4. 如果没通知 ➡️ 要约人无责 (Duty Discharged)。
MBE Contracts Review | © 2025 Exam Prep

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
On December 15, a doctor received from a retailer of office supplies an offer consisting of its catalog and a signed letter stating, "We will supply you with as many of the items in the enclosed catalog as you order during the next calendar year. We assure you that this offer and the prices in the catalog will remain firm throughout the coming year."
On January 15, having at that time received no reply from the doctor, the retailer notified the doctor that effective February 1, it was increasing the prices of certain specified items in its catalog.
Is the price increase effective with respect to catalog orders the retailer receives from the doctor during the month of February?

choices.A: No, because the retailer is a merchant with respect to office supplies; and its original offer, including the price term, was irrevocable throughout the month of February.
choices.B: No, because the retailer's original offer, including the price term, became irrevocable under the doctrine of promissory estoppel.
choices.C: Yes, because the period for which the retailer gave assurance that it would not raise prices was longer than three months.
choices.D: Yes, because the retailer received no consideration to support its assurance that it would not increase prices.

questions.explanation:
Under the UCC firm-offer rule, merchants are defined as:

  • persons who regularly deal in goods of the kind involved in the contract
  • persons who, by their occupation, hold themselves out as having knowledge or skills peculiar to the practices or goods involved or
  • any businessperson when the transaction is of a commercial nature.

A merchant's firm offer is irrevocable—and cannot be modified—for the time stated in the offer or a reasonable time if none is stated. But in no case will a firm offer remain irrevocable for more than three months.

Here, on December 15, the doctor received a catalog and a signed letter from the retailer offering to supply office supplies at the catalog prices and assuring that the offer would remain open for one year. The retailer is a merchant who regularly deals in office supplies, so its offer was firm. And although the specified time period exceeds the three-month limit, the retailer's offer is still irrevocable for three months—until March 15 (Choice C). Therefore, the retailer's attempt to increase prices was not effective with respect to February orders.

(Choice B) Under the doctrine of promissory estoppel允诺禁反言：指因合理信赖他人承诺而受损时，即使缺乏对价，承诺也应具有强制执行力的法律原则。, an offer becomes irrevocable if (1) the offeror could reasonably foresee that the offeree would rely on the offer and (2) the offeree reasonably and detrimentally relied on that offer. But here, there is no indication that the doctor relied on the retailer's offer or suffered any detriment.

(Choice D) A firm offer is irrevocable even if there is no consideration对价：英美合同法中构成有效合同所必须的要素，指双方互为交易的对给或给付。 for the assurance that the offer will be held open. Therefore, the lack of consideration does not make the retailer's price increase effective.

📌 Educational Objective

A merchant's written and signed assurance that an offer will be held open (ie, firm offer) can never exceed three months—even if the offer states that it will be held open for a longer period.

UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-205 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (firm offers).
questions.zh-question: 对于零售商在2月份收到的来自医生的目录订单，此次价格上涨是否有效？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该零售商是办公用品领域的商人；其最初的要约，包括价格条款，在整个2月份都是不可撤销的。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为根据允诺禁反言（promissory estoppel）原则，零售商的最初要约，包括价格条款，已变得不可撤销。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为零售商保证不提价的期限超过了三个月。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为零售商没有收到对价以支持其不提价的保证。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts / Sales (UCC)
⚖️ 核心规则：UCC § 2-205 Firm Offer 根据《统一商法典》(UCC)，如果商人 (Merchant) 在书面签署 (Signed Writing) 的文件中明确保证要约将保持有效，则该要约在规定期限内不可撤销 (Irrevocable)，且无需对价 (Consideration)。

⚠️ 关键限制： 如果未提供对价，不可撤销期最长不得超过 3个月。
1. 角色判定 零售商销售办公用品，属于该类商品的 Merchant。
2. 要约性质 零售商发出了书面签署的信函，并明确保证价格在一年内不变。这构成了一个 Firm Offer。
3. 时间轴计算 (考点所在)
📅 12月15日： 收到要约 (Firm Offer 开始)。
⬇️
📅 1月15日： 零售商试图提价 (撤销/修改要约)。
⬇️
📅 2月1日： 提价生效日 (目标时间点)。
⬇️
📅 3月15日： UCC规定的3个月不可撤销期届满。
虽然要约声称有效期为“一年”，但由于没有支付对价，UCC § 2-205 强制将不可撤销期限制在3个月内。
4. 结论 2月份处于12月15日开始的3个月窗口期内。在此期间，要约是绝对不可撤销的。因此，零售商单方面的提价（修改要约）无效。
为什么选 A？

选项 A 正确指出了零售商是商人，且要约在2月份期间仍处于不可撤销的状态。只要在3个月的法定上限内，Firm Offer 对商人具有约束力。

其他选项错在哪里？
陷阱 选项 C (Yes...)： 这是最常见的干扰项。虽然承诺期限超过了3个月，但这并不意味着要约立即失效或完全可撤销。法律后果是：前3个月不可撤销，3个月后要约仍然存在，但变为可撤销 (Revocable)。由于2月仍在前3个月内，所以提价无效。
基础 选项 D (Consideration)： 普通法 (Common Law) 要求期权合约 (Option Contract) 必须有对价。但本题适用 UCC，UCC 的 Firm Offer 规则是专门针对无对价情况的例外。
概念 选项 B (Promissory Estoppel)： 允诺禁反言通常用于没有正式合同或对价，但受要约人已经产生信赖利益损失的情况。本题中医生尚未回复也未采取行动（无 Detrimental Reliance），且 UCC 已有明确条文管辖，无需援引此原则。
💡 考试技巧： 看到 "Merchant" + "Signed Writing" + "Assurance"，立即反应 UCC Firm Offer。如果承诺时间 > 3个月且无对价，记住：前3个月锁死，3个月后可撤。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A college student asked her friend to lend her $2,000. The friend replied that he would do so only if the student's father, a wealthy businessman, would guarantee the loan. At the student's request, the businessman mailed a signed letter to the friend: "If you lend $2,000 to my daughter, I will repay it if she doesn't." On September 15, the friend, having read the businessman's letter, lent $2,000 to the student, which she agreed to repay in installments of $200 plus accrued interest on the last day of each month beginning October 31.
The businessman died on September 16. Later that same day, unaware of the businessman's death, the friend mailed a letter to the businessman advising that he had made the $2,000 loan to the student on September 15.
The student failed to repay any of the debt, and the entire $2,000 is due. In an action by the friend against the businessman's estate for $2,000 plus accrued interest, which of the following, if any, will serve as (an) effective defense(s) for the businessman's estate?

choices.A: The businessman died before the friend accepted his offer.
choices.B: There was no consideration to support the businessman's promise, because he did not receive any benefit.
choices.C: There was no consideration to support the businessman's promise, because he did not receive any benefit, and the businessman died before the friend notified him that his offer had been accepted.
choices.D: None of the above.

questions.explanation:
A suretyship arises when one party (guarantor) promises a second party (creditor) that the guarantor will pay the debt of a third party (principal) if he/she defaults. To be enforceable, a suretyship must be in writingMust be in writing to satisfy the Statute of Frauds (书面形式以满足欺诈法) and supported by considerationA bargained-for exchange of legal value (对价/约因). The consideration requirement is met if the guarantor is compensated for the promise. But even if the guarantor is uncompensated, the consideration requirement is still satisfied if:

  • the creditor conditioned the loan to the principal on the guarantor's promise to pay or
  • the guarantor made the promise to pay before or at the same time as the creditor made the loan to the principal.

In either case, the loan itself serves as valid consideration for the guarantor's promise—even if the guarantor is not notified when the loan is made. That is because the loan is a legal detriment to the creditor that was induced by the guarantor's promise.

Here, the friend would agree to loan the student $2,000 only on the condition that the student's father, the businessman, guarantee it. The businessman was not compensated, but he promised to guarantee the loan in writing before the friend loaned $2,000 to the student. Therefore, although the businessman died the following day before receiving notice of the loan, his promise was supported by consideration (ie, the loan to his daughter) (Choices B & C).

Additionally, a guarantor's offer to form a suretyship can be accepted by promising to give the loan or giving the loan. Here, the businessman's offer to form a suretyship was accepted when the friend loaned the student $2,000 on September 15—before the businessman died on September 16 (Choice A). As a result, none of these will serve as effective defenses for the businessman's estate.

📌 Educational Objective

A promise to guarantee a debt is supported by consideration if (1) the guarantor is compensated, (2) the loan is conditioned on obtaining a guarantee, or (3) the promise is made before or at the same time as the loan.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 88 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that a promise to guarantee a loan is binding if the promisor should reasonably expect that promise to induce the loan).
questions.zh-question:
一名大学生请求其朋友借给她2000美元。该朋友答复说，只有该学生的父亲，一位富有的商人，为这笔贷款提供担保，他才会借钱。应学生的要求，该商人向这位朋友邮寄了一封签过字的信：“如果你借给我女儿2000美元，如果她不还，我将偿还。” 9月15日，这位朋友在读了商人的信后，借给了该学生2000美元，该学生同意从10月31日开始，在每个月的最后一天分期偿还200美元及应计利息。

该商人于9月16日去世。当天晚些时候，这位朋友在不知晓该商人去世的情况下，给商人寄了一封信，告知他已于9月15日向该学生提供了2000美元的贷款。

该学生未能偿还任何债务，全部2000美元均已到期。在该朋友对该商人遗产提起的诉讼中，要求偿还2000美元及应计利息，以下哪项（如果有的话）将成为该商人遗产的有效抗辩理由？

zh-choices.A: 在朋友接受其要约之前，该商人已经去世。
zh-choices.B: 没有对价支持该商人的承诺，因为他没有获得任何利益。
zh-choices.C: 没有对价支持该商人的承诺，因为他没有获得任何利益，并且在该朋友通知他其要约已被接受之前，该商人已经去世。
zh-choices.D: 以上都不是。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts / Suretyship
正确答案：D (None of the above)

本题考查的是合同法中的保证合同（Suretyship）、对价（Consideration）以及单边合同的承诺（Acceptance）。

📅 关键时间线分析
Before Sept 15
要约 (Offer)
父亲发信承诺：“如果你借钱，我担保。”
Sept 15
承诺与合同成立 (Acceptance)
朋友借出$2,000。合同在此刻成立。
Sept 16
要约人死亡 (Death)
父亲去世。但因合同已成立，死亡不影响效力。
Sept 16 (Later)
通知 (Notice)
朋友寄出通知信。
⚖️ 核心法律解析
1. 保证合同的对价 (Consideration)
规则：保证人（父亲）不需要直接获得金钱利益。只要债权人（朋友）因保证人的承诺而遭受了法律上的不利益（Legal Detriment），即构成了有效对价。

在本案中，朋友借出$2,000本身就是一种“不利益”（Detriment）。因为朋友是基于父亲的担保承诺才同意借款的（Inducement），所以这笔贷款本身就是支持父亲担保承诺的有效对价。因此，选项 B 和 C 声称“没有对价”是错误的。

2. 单边合同的承诺 (Acceptance)

父亲的信是一个单边合同要约（Offer for a Unilateral Contract）：“如果你借钱（行为），我就担保（承诺）。”

朋友在9月15日实际借出钱款时，就是通过履行行为（Performance）完成了承诺。此时合同已经具有法律约束力。

3. 死亡对合同的影响 (Effect of Death)
规则：要约人的死亡会终止“要约”（Offer），但不会终止已经成立的“合同”（Contract）。

因为朋友在9月15日已经借款（完成了承诺），合同在父亲9月16日去世前已经成立。因此，父亲的遗产（Estate）必须履行该合同义务。选项 A 错误。

❌ 为什么其他选项是抗辩无效的？
选项 A 错误： 声称商人在朋友接受前去世。
驳斥：朋友在9月15日借款时已完成接受，商人死于9月16日。
选项 B 错误： 声称没有对价，因为商人未获益。
驳斥：保证合同中，债权人的“受损”（借出钱款）即为充分对价，无需保证人直接获益。
选项 C 错误： 结合了对价问题和通知问题。
驳斥：对价已存在（如上所述）。虽然单边合同通常需要通知，但通知是在合理时间内发出的（甚至在不知晓死亡的情况下），且缺乏通知通常只在导致保证人受损时才解除责任，并不影响合同的成立。更重要的是，题目问的是“有效抗辩”，既然合同已成立且有对价，这些都不是有效抗辩。
MBE Tip: 看到“富有的父亲为孩子担保”，首先检查是否以“贷款”作为对价。如果是，通常合同有效。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
For several weeks, a wealthy, unemployed widow and a car salesman negotiated unsuccessfully over the purchase price of a new luxury sedan, which, as the car salesman knew, the widow wanted her son to have as a wedding gift. On April 27, the salesman sent the widow a signed, dated memo saying, "If we can arrive at the same price within the next week, do we have a deal?" The widow wrote "Yes" and her signature at the bottom of this memo and delivered it back to the car salesman on April 29.
On May 1, the widow wrote the car salesman a signed letter offering to buy "one new luxury sedan, with all available equipment, for $180,000 cash on delivery not later than June 1." By coincidence, the salesman wrote the widow a signed letter on May 1 offering to sell her "one new luxury sedan, with all available equipment, for $180,000 cash on delivery not later than June 1." These letters crossed in the mail and were respectively received and read by the widow and the salesman on May 2.
If the widow subsequently asserts and the car company denies that the parties had a binding contract on May 3, which of the following most persuasively supports the widow's position?

choices.A: A sale-of-goods contract does not require that an acceptance be a mirror image of the offer.
choices.B: A sale-of-goods contract may be made in any manner sufficient to show agreement, even though the moment of its making is undetermined.
choices.C: Since the car company was a merchant in the transaction and the widow was not, the car company is estopped to deny that the parties' correspondence created a binding contract.
choices.D: With respect both to the making of an agreement and the requirement of consideration, identical cross-offers are functionally the same as an offer followed by a responsive acceptance.

questions.explanation:
Common law v. UCC
Common law UCC
Promise to hold offer open
  • Must be supported by consideration (ie, option contract)
  • No consideration required when merchant gives written & signed assurance (ie, firm offer)
Contract formation
  • Must have offer & acceptance with knowledge of that offer
  • Any manner sufficient to show agreement
Acceptance
  • Must agree to exact terms of offer (ie, mirror-image rule)
  • Effective even with new/contradictory terms
Required terms
  • Description of property/service
  • Quantity
  • Price
  • Time for performance
  • Description of goods
  • Quantity
Bilateral modification
  • Must be supported by new consideration
  • New consideration not required if made in good faith
Unilateral discharge
  • Death
  • Destruction of subject matter
  • Impracticability
Suing for breach
  • Must be in privity (ie, party to contract) or intended beneficiary
  • No privity/beneficiary requirement
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

At common law, contract formation requires (1) an offer with definite terms and (2) an acceptance with knowledge of that offer. But these formal requirements have been relaxed by the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC), which governs contracts for the sale of goods (eg, luxury sedans). Under the UCC, contract formation can occur through any manner sufficient to show the parties' agreement—even if the parties negotiate in an unusual way that makes the moment of acceptance uncertain.

Here, the widow and the car salesman agreed in writing that they would have a deal if they settled on a price for the luxury sedan within one week. Less than a week later, both parties sent identical offers that crossed in the mail, each proposing a price of $180,000. Neither party knew of the other offer when they sent their own offer (no acceptance under common law). But these cross-offers are sufficient to show that the parties arrived at the same price (agreement), which supports the widow's assertion that there was a binding contract under the UCC.

(Choice A) The UCC does not require that an acceptance be a mirror image of the offer. But this fact is irrelevant here since the two offers did mirror each other.

(Choice C) There is no rule estopping (ie, preventing) a merchant from denying that its correspondence created a binding contract.

(Choice D) An enforceable sale-of-goods contract requires consideration—ie, a bargained-for exchange of promises or performance. But the method of contract formation has nothing to do with the substance of the parties' exchange. And identical cross-offers can operate as an offer and acceptance only if the parties understood them to have the effect of forming a contract.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the UCC, a sale-of-goods contract can be made in any manner sufficient to show the parties' agreement—even if they negotiate in an unusual way that makes the moment of acceptance uncertain.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-204 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (explaining that a contract can be made in any manner sufficient to show agreement, even though the moment of its making is undetermined).
questions.zh-question: 几周以来，一位富有的失业寡妇和一位汽车销售员就一辆新的豪华轿车的购买价格进行了不成功的谈判。销售员知道，这位寡妇想把这辆车作为结婚礼物送给她的儿子。4月27日，销售员给寡妇寄去了一份签名的、注明日期的备忘录，上面写着：“如果我们在下周内能达成相同的价格，我们就算成交吗？”寡妇在这份备忘录底部写上“是”并签上自己的名字，于4月29日将其交还给汽车销售员。5月1日，寡妇给汽车销售员写了一封签名的信，提出购买“一辆新的豪华轿车，带所有可用设备，货到付款180,000美元，不迟于6月1日”。巧合的是，销售员也在5月1日给寡妇写了一封签名的信，提出向她出售“一辆新的豪华轿车，带所有可用设备，货到付款180,000美元，不迟于6月1日”。这些信件在邮寄途中交叉，寡妇和销售员分别于5月2日收到并阅读。如果寡妇随后主张而汽车公司否认双方在5月3日存在一份有约束力的合同（binding contract），以下哪项最能有力地支持寡妇的立场？

zh-choices.A: 货物买卖合同（sale-of-goods contract）不要求承诺（acceptance）是与要约（offer）完全一致的“镜像”（mirror image）。
zh-choices.B: 货物买卖合同（sale-of-goods contract）可以通过任何足以表明合意（agreement）的方式订立，即使其订立时间不确定。
zh-choices.C: 由于汽车公司在此交易中是商人（merchant）而寡妇不是，汽车公司被“禁止反言”（estopped）否认双方的通信创建了一份有约束力的合同（binding contract）。
zh-choices.D: 无论是就合意（agreement）的达成还是对对价（consideration）的要求而言，相同的交叉要约（cross-offers）在功能上等同于一个要约（offer）之后紧接着一个回应性承诺（responsive acceptance）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

合同法: 合同的成立

正确答案: B

根据UCC，货物买卖合同的成立方式可以多样，只要足以表明双方达成合意，即使合同成立的具体时间不确定也无妨。

核心法律规则：UCC下合同的成立

UCC对合同成立的灵活规定

根据《统一商法典》(Uniform Commercial Code, UCC) 第2-204条，货物买卖合同的成立比普通法(Common Law) 更为灵活，旨在促进商业交易并反映现代商业实践。UCC放宽了合同成立的严格要求，尤其是在要约和接受方面。

  • 合意方式的灵活性：UCC规定，货物买卖合同可以通过任何足以表明双方达成合意的方式来成立，包括口头、书面或行为。即使双方的谈判过程不寻常，或者合同成立的确切时间无法确定，也不影响其有效性。关键在于是否存在“合意”(agreement)。
  • “镜像规则”的放松：与普通法严格的“镜像规则”(mirror-image rule) 不同，UCC下，接受条款即使包含附加或不同的条款，也可能构成有效接受，除非明确规定接受必须严格符合要约。
  • 要约与接受的非必需性：即使没有明确的要约(offer) 和接受(acceptance)，只要双方的行为或书面往来足以表明他们意图订立合同，并且存在合理确定的履行基础，合同即可成立。

概念对比：普通法与UCC下合同成立

合同成立要素 普通法 (Common Law) UCC (统一商法典)
要约保持开放的承诺
(Promise to hold offer open)		 必须有对价(consideration) 支持 (例如，期权合同 option contract)。 当商人(merchant) 给出书面并签署的保证时，无需对价 (例如，确定要约 firm offer)。
合同成立
(Contract formation)		 必须有要约和接受，且双方知晓该要约。 任何足以表明合意的方式即可。
接受
(Acceptance)		 必须同意要约的精确条款 (即，“镜像规则” mirror-image rule)。 即使包含新的/矛盾的条款也有效。
必要条款
(Required terms)		 财产/服务描述、数量、价格、履行时间。 货物描述、数量。
双边修改
(Bilateral modification)		 必须有新的对价支持。 如果出于善意，无需新的对价。
单方解除
(Unilateral discharge)		 死亡、标的物毁坏。 不可行性(impracticability)。
起诉违约
(Suing for breach)		 必须有合同关系(privity) (即，合同当事人) 或预期受益人。 无合同关系/受益人要求。

案情分析与适用

本案涉及一位富有的寡妇和一位汽车销售员之间关于购买一辆豪华轿车的交易。由于这是一笔货物（豪华轿车）的买卖，因此适用《统一商法典》(UCC)。

  1. 初步谈判与意向：双方在4月27日和29日通过备忘录确认了“如果在一周内达成相同价格，就成交”的意向，这表明了双方有订立合同的初步意愿。
  2. 交叉要约的出现：5月1日，寡妇和销售员在不知情的情况下，各自发出了内容完全相同的书面要约，以18万美元的价格购买/出售同一辆豪华轿车，并于5月2日收到。
  3. 普通法下的问题：在普通法下，由于双方在发出各自的要约时都不知道对方的要约，因此不存在传统意义上的“要约与接受”以及“对要约的知晓”，这通常无法构成合同。
  4. UCC下的解决方案：然而，UCC对合同成立的规定更为宽松。尽管这些是交叉要约，但它们的内容完全一致，且双方都收到了对方的要约。这些书面往来足以表明双方在5月1日（或最迟5月2日收到时）就豪华轿车的买卖达成了合意，价格为18万美元。UCC允许合同以“任何足以表明合意的方式”成立，即使成立时间不确定。因此，寡妇主张存在约束性合同的立场得到了UCC的有力支持。

事件流程图

谈判数周
↓
4月27日: 销售员发出备忘录 ("若一周内同价，则成交？")
↓
4月29日: 寡妇在备忘录上签署"Yes"并返还
↓
5月1日: 寡妇和销售员各自发出相同内容的要约 (18万美元)
↓
5月2日: 双方收到对方的要约 (交叉要约)
↓
5月3日: 寡妇主张存在约束性合同
↓
UCC: 交叉要约足以表明合意，合同成立

MBE 陷阱提示：普通法与UCC的区分

本题的关键在于区分普通法和UCC下合同成立规则的差异。普通法要求严格的“镜像规则”和对要约的知晓，而UCC则强调“合意”的实质，允许更灵活的合同成立方式。当题目涉及货物买卖时，应优先考虑UCC的规定，避免被普通法的严格要求所误导。

正确答案与干扰项排除

B. 货物买卖合同可以通过任何足以表明合意的方式成立，即使合同成立的具体时间不确定也无妨。

正确。 这正是UCC第2-204条的核心原则。本案中，双方在同一时间各自发出内容完全相同的要约，虽然不是传统意义上的“要约-接受”模式，但这些交叉要约明确表明了双方在价格和标的物上达成了合意。UCC的灵活性使得这种非传统的合意方式也能构成有效合同。

A. 货物买卖合同不要求接受是要约的镜像。

错误。 尽管UCC确实不要求严格的“镜像规则”，但本案中双方的交叉要约内容实际上是完全一致的，即它们“镜像”了彼此。因此，这个选项虽然陈述的法律原则正确，但它并非最能说服性地支持寡妇立场的理由，因为它没有解决“交叉要约”这种特殊形成方式的问题，也没有强调UCC在合意方式上的整体灵活性。

C. 由于汽车公司是交易中的商人而寡妇不是，汽车公司被禁止否认双方的往来信件构成了约束性合同。

错误。 法律中没有普遍的规则禁止商人否认其往来信件构成了约束性合同。虽然UCC对商人有特殊规则（如“确定要约”），但本案中没有适用禁止反言(estoppel) 的直接理由来强制合同成立。合同的成立是基于双方的合意，而非单方被禁止否认。

D. 无论是在达成协议还是对价要求方面，相同的交叉要约在功能上与要约后跟一个回应性接受相同。

错误。 尽管在UCC下，相同的交叉要约可能表明合意，但它们在功能上并非总是与传统的“要约-接受”模式完全相同，尤其是在对价(consideration) 方面。对价是合同的实质性要素，而交叉要约只是合同成立的“方式”问题。此外，交叉要约能否构成合同，还取决于双方是否理解它们具有形成合同的效力。这个选项混淆了合同成立的方式与对价的实质要求，且其表述过于绝对。

MBE 考试技巧：UCC的“合意”优先原则

在MBE考试中，遇到货物买卖合同的成立问题时，请记住UCC的核心精神是促进商业交易。这意味着只要有足够的证据表明双方有订立合同的意图和合意，即使形式不完美、时间不确定，或者存在交叉要约等非传统情况，合同也可能成立。UCC更关注交易的实质而非严格的形式主义。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A distributor of industrial products was unhappy with the quality of its previous supplier's heavy-duty electric wall sockets. On April 7, the distributor reached out to a new supplier in an email that stated in its entirety: "Offer to purchase as many industrial straight-blade sockets as you can supply for delivery by May 6." That same day, the supplier responded to the distributor, "Order received. Delivery by May 7."
The supplier sent the distributor 200 of the only industrial straight-blade sockets it carried, at $1 over market price per unit, payment due on delivery. The distributor took delivery of the sockets on May 7 but rejected them without stating any basis for doing so.
If the new supplier sues the distributor for breach of contract, will the supplier be likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the quantity of sockets was not specified.
choices.B: No, because the supplier's response contained a different delivery date than the offer.
choices.C: Yes, because the court will apply UCC gap-fillers when the quantity of goods is not specified.
choices.D: Yes, because the offer included a means for determining the quantity of sockets to be sold.

questions.explanation:
Contract terms must be sufficiently certain and definite for the court to determine the existence of a breach and give an appropriate remedy. While the common law requires that all essential terms be covered in the agreement,* the UCC—which governs contracts for the sale of goods (eg, sockets)—is more liberal. It encourages contract formation by providing "gap-fillers" for many missing terms, but not the:

  • identity of the contracting parties
  • subject matter of the contract or
  • quantity of goods to be sold (Choice C).

A contract must therefore specify a quantity that is certain or determinable by reference to objective facts, such as the buyer's actual requirements or the seller's actual output in a requirements or output contract. If it does not, the contract fails for indefiniteness.

Here, the parties did not specify the exact quantity of sockets to be sold (Choice A). However, the distributor offered to purchase as many straight-blade sockets as the supplier could supply by May 6. This provides a quantity term that is determinable by reference to objective facts, such as the supplier's inventory between the date the offer was received and May 6. Therefore, the supplier is likely to prevail in a breach-of-contract suit.

*The omission of an essential term is not necessarily fatal if it appears that the parties intended to form a binding agreement. When this occurs, the court can look to the surrounding circumstances and the parties' conduct to fill in the term.

(Choice B) Under the UCC, parties can form a contract even if the offer and the acceptance include different terms. When both parties are merchants (as seen here), most jurisdictions will "knock out" the differing terms and replace them with UCC gap-fillers as needed. Therefore, the differing delivery dates will be knocked out and delivery will be required within a reasonable time.

📌 Educational Objective

The UCC "fills the gap" for missing contract terms other than the parties, subject matter, and quantity. The quantity term must specify an amount that is certain or capable of being made certain by reference to objective facts.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-201 cmt. 1 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (required terms for contracts for sale of goods).
  • U.C.C. §§ 2-305–2-310 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (UCC gap-fillers).
questions.zh-question:
一家工业产品经销商对其前供应商的重型墙壁电源插座的质量感到不满。4月7日，该经销商通过一封电子邮件联系了一家新供应商，邮件全文如下：“要约购买工业直片插座，要求于5月6日前交货。”同日，供应商回复经销商：“订单收到。5月7日交货。”

供应商向经销商发送了其唯一销售的200个工业直片插座，单价比市场价高出1美元，货到付款。经销商于5月7日收到了插座，但未说明任何理由即予以拒收。

如果新供应商以违约为由起诉经销商，供应商是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为插座的数量未被明确，并且没有其他方法来确定这一基本条款。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为在经销商对价格保持沉默的情况下，双方并未就插座的单价达成合意。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为当数量未明确时，法院将认定合同存在，并以交付的合理数量为准。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为根据“剔除规则”(knockout rule)，法院将取消双方冲突的交货条款，并推定一个合理的交货时间。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts / UCC Formation

正确答案：A
✅ 核心结论

供应商无法胜诉。因为合同缺少必要的数量条款 (Quantity Term)，导致合同因不确定 (Indefiniteness) 而无法成立。

法律规则 (The Rule)
⚖️ UCC 的“填补空白”规则

本案涉及货物买卖，适用 Uniform Commercial Code (UCC)。

UCC 旨在促成交易，因此对于许多缺失的条款（Missing Terms），法律允许法院使用“填补规则” (Gap Fillers) 来补充，例如：

  • 💰 价格 (Price)： 若未约定，视为交付时的合理价格。
  • 🚚 交付 (Delivery)： 若未约定，视为合理时间、卖方营业地交付。
  • 💳 付款 (Payment)： 若未约定，视为收货时付款。

⚠️ 致命例外：数量 (Quantity)
UCC 不会填补数量条款。如果合同没有明确数量，或者没有提供计算数量的客观方法（如需求合同 Requirements Contract），则合同不成立。

🔍 案情应用

在本案中，经销商的邮件仅写道：“Offer to purchase industrial straight-blade sockets”（要约购买工业直片插座）。

  • 它没有说“购买 100 个” (Specific Quantity)。
  • 它也没有说“购买我所需要的所有插座” (Requirements Contract)。

由于数量完全缺失，法院无法确定违约赔偿的基数。因此，尽管卖方发货了，但双方并未形成具有法律约束力的合同。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？
  • 选项 B (价格缺失)： 错误。如前所述，UCC 可以填补价格条款 (Reasonable Price)，价格缺失不会导致合同无效。
  • 选项 C (合理数量)： 错误。这是考生常犯的错误。法院不会凭空捏造一个“合理数量”来挽救合同。没有数量 = 没有合同。
  • 选项 D (剔除规则 Knockout Rule)： 错误。剔除规则用于解决双方格式条款冲突的问题 (Battle of the Forms, UCC § 2-207)。但在使用该规则前，必须先有一个有效的合同。本案因缺数量连合同都没成立，自然谈不上剔除条款。

💡 MBE 提分技巧：
看到 UCC 合同题目，首先检查 Quantity (数量)。
如果数量缺失且不是 Output/Requirements Contract，
直接选“合同不成立”。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A bottling company sent a purchase order to a wholesaler that stated, "Ship 100,000 empty plastic bottles at the posted price." Two days after receipt of this purchase order, the wholesaler shipped the bottles and the bottling company accepted delivery of them. A week after the bottles were delivered, the bottling company received the wholesaler's acknowledgment form, which included a provision disclaiming consequential damages. After having used the wholesaler's bottles in its bottling operations for two months, the bottling company discovered a defect in the bottles that caused liquids to leak from them. The bottling company recalled 10,000 of the bottles that had been filled, incurring lost profits of $40,000.
Assuming that all appropriate defenses are timely raised, will the bottling company likely succeed in recovering $40,000 in consequential damages from the wholesaler?

choices.A: No, because buyers are generally not entitled to recover consequential damages.
choices.B: No, because the bottling company's acceptance of the goods also constituted an acceptance of the terms included in the wholesaler's acknowledgment.
choices.C: Yes, because the disclaimer of consequential damages is unconscionable.
choices.D: Yes, because the wholesaler's acknowledgment did not alter the terms of an existing contract between the parties.

questions.explanation:
Seller's acceptance of buyer's offer
(UCC § 2-206)
Method Effective Contract terms
Promise to ship
  • When oral promise made OR
  • When written promise sent
  • All parties are merchants
    • terms of offer +
    • terms added by battle-of-forms rule
  • ≥1 party is nonmerchant
    • terms of offer
    • new terms are merely proposed additions
Shipment of goods
  • When goods shipped
  • Terms of offer
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

Under the UCC, a seller can accept an offer (eg, purchase order) by shipping or promising to ship the ordered goods. Acceptance by shipment is effective immediately and creates a contract with terms identical to those of the offer. Once created, the contract cannot be modified unless both parties agree to this. And if either party breaches, the other party can recover consequential damages (eg, lost profits).

Here, the wholesaler received the bottling company's purchase order and shipped the bottles. That shipment—since it was sent before the acknowledgment form—created a contract on the purchase order's terms. And since the bottling company did not agree to a modification that disclaims consequential damages, the acknowledgment did not alter the terms of the existing contract. Therefore, the bottling company will likely recover $40,000 in consequential damages for its lost profits caused by the wholesaler's breach in sending defective bottles.

(Choice A) Either party to a sale-of-goods contract (ie, buyer or seller) can recover consequential damages for breach as long as those damages were foreseeable when the contract was created.

(Choice B) The bottling company's acceptance of the bottles could not have constituted an acceptance of the terms included in the wholesaler's acknowledgment since the bottles were delivered and accepted before the acknowledgment was received.

(Choice C) A contract can limit or disclaim (ie, exclude) consequential damages unless doing so is unconscionable because it leaves no reasonable remedy for breach. But here, whether the disclaimer of consequential damages is unconscionable is irrelevant since that term did not become part of the contract.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the UCC, a seller can accept an offer to buy goods by shipping or promising to ship the goods. Acceptance by shipment is effective immediately and creates a contract with terms identical to those of the offer.

UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-206 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (explaining that an offer to buy goods can be accepted by shipping or promising to ship the goods).
questions.zh-question:
一家装瓶公司向一家批发商发送了一份采购订单，订单中写明：“请以挂牌价运送10万个空塑料瓶。”收到此采购订单两天后，该批发商发运了这批瓶子，装瓶公司接受了交付。瓶子交付一周后，装瓶公司收到了批发商的确认函，其中包含一条免除间接损害赔偿责任的条款。在将批发商的瓶子用于其装瓶作业两个月后，装瓶公司发现瓶子存在缺陷，导致液体泄漏。装瓶公司召回了1万个已灌装的瓶子，造成了4万美元的利润损失。

假设所有适当的抗辩都已及时提出，装瓶公司是否可能成功地从批发商处获得4万美元的间接损害赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为买方通常无权获得间接损害赔偿。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为装瓶公司对货物的接受也构成了对批发商确认函中所含条款的接受。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为免除间接损害赔偿责任的条款是不合情理的。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为批发商的确认函并未改变双方之间现有合同的条款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析
UCC 合同成立与条款变更

核心考点 (Key Rule):
根据《统一商法典》(UCC) § 2-206，卖方可以通过发货 (Shipment) 来接受买方的购买要约。一旦发货，合同即告成立，条款以要约（采购订单）为准。
📅 案情时间轴分析
Day 1
买方发出采购订单 (Offer)
条款：数量、价格。
注意：此时没有免责条款。
Day 3 (收到后两天)
卖方发货 (Shipment)
★ 关键点：合同在此刻成立！
根据 UCC § 2-206(1)(b)，迅速发货构成承诺 (Acceptance)。
Day 10 (发货后一周)
卖方发送确认函 (Acknowledgment)
包含免除间接损害赔偿 (Disclaimer) 条款。
法律定性：这是修改合同的提议 (Proposal for Modification)，而非反要约。
⚖️ 法律推理 (Legal Reasoning)

本题的陷阱在于“格式之争” (Battle of the Forms, UCC § 2-207) 的适用时机。

通常，如果卖方先发确认函（包含新条款），再发货，我们需要分析新条款是否进入合同。但本案中，发货发生在确认函之前。

  • 当卖方发货时，合同已经锁定。条款=采购订单的条款。
  • 一周后收到的确认函，试图增加“免责条款”。根据 UCC § 2-209，这属于对已存在合同的修改 (Modification)。
  • 修改合同需要双方同意。买方从未同意该免责条款，因此该条款无效。
✅ 为什么选 D？
选项 D 正确：
因为批发商的确认函（Acknowledgment）并没有改变双方之间现有合同的条款。

解析：既然合同在发货时已经成立（且不包含免责条款），后来的确认函只是一张试图修改合同的废纸，除非买方明确同意修改，否则其中的免责条款不生效。买方有权根据 UCC 获得间接损害赔偿 (Consequential Damages)。
❌ 其他选项为何错误？
选项 A 错误：
UCC 明确允许买方在卖方违约时获得间接损害赔偿 (UCC § 2-715)，只要这些损失是可预见的 (Foreseeable)。
选项 B 错误：
买方接受货物是对货物本身的接受，并不代表接受了一周后才收到的文件中的条款。接受货物时，那份确认函甚至还没寄到。
选项 C 错误：
虽然“显失公平” (Unconscionability) 是一个有效的抗辩理由，但在这里我们不需要用到它。因为该条款根本就没有进入合同，所以无需讨论它是否显失公平。
🎓 考试技巧 (Exam Tip):
在处理 UCC 合同形成题目时，务必关注时间顺序！
如果是“先发货，后发单据”，合同通常以买方订单条款为准成立。如果是“先发单据（含新条款），后发货”，则需要进行复杂的 UCC § 2-207 分析。
MBE Contracts Review

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A business contracted in writing with a shareholder who owned all of a corporation's outstanding stock to purchase the stock at a specified price per share. At the time this contract was executed, the business's contracting officer said to the shareholder, "Of course, our commitment to buy is conditioned on our obtaining approval of the contract from our parent company." The shareholder replied, "Fine. No problem." The parent company orally approved the contract, but the shareholder changed her mind and refused to consummate the sale on two grounds: (1) when the agreement was made there was no consideration for her promise to sell; and (2) the parent company's approval of the contract was invalid.
If the business sues the shareholder for breach of contract, is the business likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because mutuality of obligation between the parties was lacking when the agreement was made.
choices.B: No, because the condition of the parent company's approval of the contract was an essential part of the agreed exchange and was not in a signed writing.
choices.C: Yes, because any possible lack of consideration for the shareholder's promise to sell was expressly waived by the shareholder when the agreement was made.
choices.D: Yes, because the business's promise to buy, bargained for and made in exchange for the shareholder's promise to sell, was good consideration even though it was expressly conditioned on an event that was not certain to occur.

questions.explanation:
Elements of valuable consideration
Bargained-for exchange Each party's willingness to enter agreement must be induced by other party's act/promise
Legal detriment Each party must relinquish legal right by either:
  • performing (or promising to perform) act that is not legally required or
  • refraining (or promising to refrain) from performing legally permissible act

A contract is a legally enforceable agreement that is created when a mutual agreement is supported by valuable consideration—ie, a bargained-for exchange of promises or performance. However, performance can be delayed or discharged by a condition—ie, an uncertain future event that must occur before performance becomes due or is discharged. There are two types of conditions:

  • Condition precedent* – delays performance until a specified event occurs
  • Condition subsequent – excuses performance once a specified event occurs

Here, the business promised to purchase, and the shareholder promised to sell, all of the shareholder's stock in a corporation. This exchange of promises provided valuable consideration to form a valid contract. But the parties' performance of that contract was contingent upon the business obtaining approval of the agreement from its parent company—a condition precedent. Since that condition precedent was met when the parent company approved the purchase, the business would likely prevail in a breach-of-contract action based on the shareholder's refusal to sell.

*A condition concurrent arises when each party's obligation to perform is a condition precedent to the other party's obligation to perform (ie, when performance is due simultaneously).

(Choices A & C) Mutuality of obligation between the parties was not lacking, and their agreement was supported by consideration, because the business's promise to purchase stock was induced by the shareholder's promise to sell it (and vice versa).

(Choice B) There is no rule requiring that a condition be included in a signed writing.

📌 Educational Objective

A contract is generally formed when a mutual agreement is supported by valuable consideration and may include conditions that delay (condition precedent) or excuse (condition subsequent) a party's promised performance.
questions.zh-question:
一家企业与一名拥有某公司全部流通股的股东签订书面合同，以约定的每股价格购买该股票。在合同签署时，该企业的签约代表对股东说：“当然，我们购买的承诺，是以我们获得母公司对该合同的批准为条件的。”股东回答说：“好的，没问题。”母公司口头批准了该合同，但股东改变了主意，并以两个理由拒绝完成该交易：(1) 协议达成时，她出售的承诺没有对价；(2) 母公司对合同的批准无效。

如果该企业以违约为由起诉该股东，企业是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为在协议达成时，双方之间缺乏相互义务。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为母公司批准合同的条件是约定交换的重要组成部分，且未以签署的书面形式存在。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为在协议达成时，股东明确放弃了其出售承诺可能存在的任何对价缺失问题。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该企业购买的承诺，是为换取股东出售的承诺而进行的交易磋商，即使该承诺明确地以一个不确定会发生的事件为条件，它也是有效的对价。

MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Consideration & Conditions
核心法律原则

即使承诺是附条件的 (Conditional Promise)，只要该条件不是完全由承诺人随意控制（即不是虚幻承诺 Illusory Promise），该承诺依然构成有效的对价 (Consideration)。

Business
承诺购买
(条件：母公司批准)
⇄
Shareholder
承诺出售
(无条件)

双方存在“交易磋商的交换” (Bargained-for Exchange)

为什么选 D？
正确逻辑

本题的关键在于判断“附条件的承诺”是否足以构成对价。

  • 法律规则：如果一方的承诺以某个事件的发生为条件（Condition Precedent），只要该事件有可能发生，且不在该方的完全随意控制之下，那么这个承诺就是一种法律上的“受损” (Legal Detriment)，因此构成有效对价。
  • 本案应用：企业承诺购买股票，条件是“母公司批准”。虽然这看起来给了企业退路，但法律通常认为寻求第三方（母公司）批准包含着善意 (Good Faith) 的义务，并非企业可以随意取消。
  • 因此，企业的承诺不是虚幻的，它与股东的出售承诺构成了有效的交换。
干扰项排除
选项 A 错误

Mutuality of obligation (义务的相互性) 并未缺失。虽然企业的义务是附条件的，但一旦条件满足（母公司批准），企业就必须履行。这种潜在的约束力足以满足相互性的要求。

选项 B 错误

Condition (条件) 不一定非要写在签署的文件中才有效。口头约定的先决条件（Condition Precedent to Effectiveness）通常是允许的，甚至在有书面合同时，根据口头证据规则 (Parol Evidence Rule) 的例外，往往也可以引入证据证明该条件的存在。更重要的是，本案中条件已经发生（母公司已批准），所以合同已经生效。

选项 C 错误

不需要讨论“放弃对价” (Waiver of Consideration)。因为对价本身就是存在的，不需要被放弃。

💡 MBE 提分技巧

在 Contracts 题目中，当看到一方说“如果 X 发生，我就做 Y”时：

  1. 检查 X 是否完全由该方随意控制（例如“如果我想买”）。如果是，这是 Illusory Promise，无对价。
  2. 如果 X 是客观事件或涉及第三方（如“如果银行批准贷款”、“如果母公司批准”），这是 Valid Conditional Promise，有对价。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
An entrepreneur owed his neighbor $1,000, plus interest at 8% until paid, on a long-overdue promissory note, collection of which would become barred by the statute of limitations on June 30. On the preceding April 1, the entrepreneur and the neighbor both signed a writing in which the entrepreneur promised to pay the note in full on the following December 31, plus interest at 8% until that date, and the neighbor promised not to sue on the note in the meantime. The neighbor, having received some advice from his nonlawyer brother-in-law, became concerned about the legal effect of the April 1 agreement. On May 1, acting pro se as permitted by the rules of the local small claims court, the neighbor filed suit to collect the note.
Assuming that there is no controlling statute, is the April 1 agreement an effective defense for the entrepreneur?

choices.A: No, because the entrepreneur's April 1 promise is enforceable with or without consideration.
choices.B: No, because there was no consideration for the neighbor's promise not to sue, in that the entrepreneur was already obligated to pay $1,000 plus interest at 8% until the payment date.
choices.C: Yes, because the entrepreneur's promise to pay interest until December 31 was consideration for the neighbor's promise not to sue.
choices.D: Yes, because the law creates a presumption that the entrepreneur relied on the neighbor's promise not to sue.

questions.explanation:
Exceptions to preexisting-duty rule
Main rule Promise to perform (or performance of) preexisting duty is not consideration
Common-law exceptions New/altered consideration New duty added or preexisting duty altered (eg, acceleration of due date)
Ratification of voidable duty New promise to perform voidable duty (eg, upon reaching age of majority)
Honest dispute Scope of duty honestly disputed
Unexpected event Fair & equitable modification in view of unanticipated circumstances
Renewed promise Renewed promise to pay preexisting debt despite technical defense (eg, statute of limitations, bankruptcy) if written or partially performed
Third party Third party offers additional promise that is contingent on performance of preexisting duty
UCC exception Modification Modification sought in good faith—ie, honesty and observance of reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

A valid claim can be permanently or temporarily settled by entering a written settlement agreement in which each party's promise or performance is consideration (ie, exchanged) for the other party's promise or performance. A promise to perform (or the performance of) a preexisting contractual duty is generally not consideration. But if the duty is altered in any way (eg, acceleration of a due date), there is consideration, and the agreement will provide an effective defense in a lawsuit that asserts the settled claim.

Here, the entrepreneur owed the neighbor $1,000 plus 8% interest until paid. On April 1, they signed a settlement agreement in which the entrepreneur promised to repay the debt by December 31. Although the entrepreneur was already obligated to pay 8% interest, the new due date altered his duties (Choice B). As a result, the entrepreneur's promise was consideration for the neighbor's promise not to sue before December 31. Since the neighbor sued before then (on May 1), the April 1 agreement is an effective defense for the entrepreneur.

(Choice A) The entrepreneur's April 1 promise to repay the debt by December 31 would be unenforceable without consideration. But that promise is supported by consideration—ie, the neighbor's return promise not to sue before December 31.

(Choice D) Under the doctrine of promissory estoppel, a promise can become enforceable if the promisee (eg, the entrepreneur) proves that he/she reasonably and detrimentally relied on that promise. But the promisee's reliance will not be presumed.

📌 Educational Objective

A promise to perform (or the performance of) a preexisting contractual duty is not consideration unless that duty is altered in some way (eg, acceleration of a due date).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 74 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (settlement of claims).

一名企业家根据一张逾期已久的本票，欠其邻居1,000美元，外加年利率8%的利息，直至付清为止。该本票的追偿将于6月30日因诉讼时效届满而被禁止。在之前的4月1日，该企业家和邻居共同签署了一份书面文件，其中企业家承诺在接下来的12月31日全额支付该本票，并支付截至该日的8%利息；而邻居则承诺在此期间不对该本票提起诉讼。邻居在听取了其非律师身份的姐夫/妹夫的一些建议后，开始担心4月1日协议的法律效力。5月1日，邻居根据当地小额索赔法院规则的许可，自行代理诉讼以追讨该本票。

假设没有管辖性法规，4月1日的协议对该企业家而言是否构成有效的抗辩？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为无论有无对价，该企业家4月1日的承诺都是可强制执行的。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为邻居不起诉的承诺没有对价，原因是该企业家本已有义务支付1,000美元及截至付款之日的8%利息。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该企业家承诺支付利息至12月31日，这是对邻居不起诉承诺的对价。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为法律创设了一项推定，即该企业家信赖了邻居不起诉的承诺。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts / Consideration

Correct Answer
选项 C (Yes)

4月1日的协议对企业家构成了有效抗辩。

核心逻辑：为什么这属于“新对价”？

考生常误认为企业家只是承诺了“本来就要付的利息”。但根据 Preexisting Duty Rule，该协议引入了两个关键的法律变更：

  • 时效重置：原债务在 6月30日 后将因诉讼时效届满而失去强制执行力。企业家承诺支付到 12月31日的利息，意味着他承诺了法律本将豁免的额外利息。
  • 权利放弃：原合同是“利息计至付清时”，债务人本可随时还钱以停止利息。新协议锁定了 12月31日，他放弃了通过提前还款来节省利息的权利。
法律义务时间轴
原债务 (Original Debt)
义务止于还款日，且最晚止于
6月30日 (诉讼时效届满)
⬇️ 4月1日签署新协议 ⬇️
新协议 (New Agreement)
企业家承诺：利息强制计算至 12月31日
(超出的6个月利息即为“新对价”)
法律分析

在法律上，只要存在任何形式的法律受损 (Legal Detriment)，即视为有对价。

1. 邻居的法律受损：承诺在12月31日前放弃起诉的权利。
2. 企业家的法律受损：承诺支付原本在6月30日后就不再受法律保护的本金及利息，并放弃了提前还款权。

由于双方均提供了新对价，该协议是一份有效的合同修改，邻居在5月1日起诉违反了协议，因此企业家可以据此抗辩。

为什么 B 是干扰项？

选项 B 认为这只是“履行已存义务”。但它忽略了：诉讼时效即将届满 这一事实改变了义务的本质。在普通法下，对一个带有技术性防御（如时效、破产）的旧债做出新的书面还款承诺，本身就具有法律效力，若再伴随计息期的延长，对价则更加充分。

💡 考试避坑指南

只要看到还款日期被固定或计息方式被改变，通常就存在新对价。不要简单地看到“金额没变”或“利率没变”就选无对价。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A niece had worked in her aunt's bookstore for many years. The bookstore business, which was housed in a building that the aunt leased, was independently appraised at $200,000. The aunt decided to retire. She wrote to the niece, expressing her affection for the niece and offering to sell her the bookstore business for $125,000 if the landlord would agree to a transfer of the lease. The letter also specified when the aunt would transfer the business. The niece wrote back accepting her aunt's offer. In a phone call to the niece, the aunt stated that the landlord had approved the transfer of the lease and that she would now ask her attorney to draft a written contract so that there would be a record of the terms. Before the attorney had finished drafting the document, the aunt changed her mind about selling the business and informed the niece of her decision.
In an action for breach of contract brought by the niece against her aunt, is the niece likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the motivation for the transfer of the business was the aunt's affection for her niece, not the price.
choices.B: No, because the promised consideration was inadequate in light of the market value of the business.
choices.C: Yes, because the condition concerning the landlord's assent to the transfer of the lease was beyond the control of either party.
choices.D: Yes, because the document being drafted by the attorney was merely a record of an agreement already made, not a condition to it.

questions.explanation:
Contract conditions
Condition precedent Uncertain future event that, if it occurs, creates party's obligation to perform (e.g., A agrees to hire B if B graduates college)
Condition subsequent Uncertain future event that, if it occurs, excuses party's existing obligation to perform (e.g., B agrees to work for C until B graduates college)

A binding contract is formed when one party (ie, the offeror) makes an offer and the other party (ie, the offeree) accepts it. The resulting contract can contain certain conditions affecting the parties' duty to perform:

  • condition precedent – an uncertain future event that, if it occurs, creates a party's duty to perform
  • condition subsequent – an uncertain future event that, if it occurs, excuses a party's existing duty to perform

Here, the niece accepted the aunt's offer to sell the bookstore for $125,000 if the landlord agreed to transfer the lease. This created a condition precedent that triggered the aunt's duty to perform once the landlord agreed to the transfer. The aunt then told the niece that she would ask her attorney to draft a written contract. But this did not create a condition because conditions cannot be added unilaterally after contract formation.

Additionally, the parties' agreement to memorialize the contract in a final writing after a binding contract had been formed does not prevent enforcement of their original informal agreement. This is true even if the contemplated writing is never prepared. Therefore, the niece is likely to prevail in her breach of contract action.

(Choice A & B) Contracts must be supported by valuable consideration—ie, a bargained-for exchange of promises or performance. Here, the aunt's promise to sell her business and the niece's promise to pay $125,000 constituted the necessary bargained-for exchange—even if the aunt was partially motivated by affection. And since equivalence in value is not required, it does not matter that the business is worth $200,000.

(Choice C) Contracts are often conditioned on events that are beyond the control of either party (eg, the landlord's assent to the transfer of the lease), and this fact has no effect on the outcome of this dispute.

📌 Educational Objective

Once a binding contract is formed, the fact that the parties further agree that the contract will be memorialized in a final writing does not prevent enforcement of the original agreement—even if the writing is never prepared.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 27 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (existence of contract where written memorial is contemplated).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 224–25 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (defining and explaining contract conditions).
questions.zh-question:
一位侄女在其姑妈的书店工作多年。该书店业务位于姑妈租赁的一栋建筑内，经独立评估，价值为20万美元。姑妈决定退休。她写信给侄女，表达了对侄女的喜爱，并要约以12.5万美元的价格将书店业务出售给她，条件是房东同意转让租约。信中还明确了姑妈转让业务的时间。侄女回信接受了姑妈的要约。在给侄女的一通电话中，姑妈表示房东已批准租约转让，她现在将请她的律师起草一份书面合同，以便对条款进行记录。在该律师完成文件起草之前，姑妈改变了出售业务的想法，并将她的决定告知了侄女。

在侄女对姑妈提起的违约诉讼中，侄女是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为转让业务的动机是姑妈对侄女的喜爱，而非价格。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为与业务的市场价值相比，所承诺的对价不足。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为关于房东同意转让租约的条件超出了任何一方的控制范围。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为律师正在起草的文件仅仅是对已达成协议的记录，而非协议的一项条件。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

合同成立与书面记录
Formation & Memorialization

核心法律规则

本题考察的核心在于区分以下两种情况：

  1. 合同成立后的书面记录 (Memorialization of an agreement)：双方已经达成合意，只是想把条款写下来留底。此时，口头或非正式协议已经具有约束力。
  2. 以签署书面合同为生效条件 (Condition of validity)：双方明确表示，在正式书面合同签署之前，不受任何约束。

规则：除非双方明确表示在正式文件签署前不承担义务，否则只要对所有主要条款达成一致，合同即告成立。后续的起草工作仅仅是“记录” (Record)，而非“条件” (Condition)。

✅ 为什么选 D？

选项 D 正确。

在本案中，合同成立的时间线如下：

  • 要约 (Offer)： 姑妈写信提出以 $125,000 出售，并设定了条件（房东同意）。
  • 承诺 (Acceptance)： 侄女回信接受。此时双方达成合意 (Mutual Assent)。
  • 先决条件成就 (Condition Precedent Met)： 房东批准了租约转让。此时合同已完全生效。

姑妈随后提到找律师起草合同，目的是“为了对条款进行记录” (so that there would be a record)。这表明书面文件只是为了证据保存 (Evidentiary purpose)，而不是合同成立的新条件。

因此，即使书面文件未完成，之前的协议依然有效且可执行。

❌ 为什么排除其他选项？

选项 A：动机 (Motivation)

错误。虽然姑妈是出于喜爱（Affection），但只要存在经过讨价还价的交换 (Bargained-for exchange)，即“书店业务”交换“$125,000”，合同就成立。动机不影响对价 (Consideration) 的有效性。

选项 B：对价是否充分 (Adequacy of Consideration)

错误。普通法的一般原则是法院不审查对价的充分性 (Courts do not inquire into the adequacy of consideration)。只要不是象征性的虚假对价（如“1美元”），$125,000 购买价值 $200,000 的资产是完全有效的交易。

选项 C：不可控条件 (Condition beyond control)

错误。虽然房东是否同意确实超出了双方控制，但这只是一个先决条件 (Condition Precedent)。题目明确指出房东已经批准了。一旦条件满足，合同义务就被激活。这个事实支持合同有效，而不是反对。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

在处理涉及“后续书面合同” (Subsequent Written Contract) 的题目时，请寻找关键词：

  • 如果题目说 "subject to a signed contract" 或 "not binding until signed"，则书面形式是条件。
  • 如果题目说 "to memorialize"、"to keep a record" 或 "formalize the agreement"，通常意味着合同已经成立，后续文书工作不影响其效力。

记住：合同法倾向于保护双方已达成的合意 (Intent of the parties)。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A debtor's liquidated and undisputed $1,000 debt to a creditor was due on March 1. When the debt was still unpaid on March 15, the creditor told the debtor that if the debtor promised to pay the $1,000 on or before December 1, the creditor would then not sue to collect the debt. The debtor orally agreed. On April 1, the creditor sued the debtor to collect the debt that had become due on March 1. The debtor moved to dismiss the creditor's complaint.
Should the court grant the debtor's motion?

choices.A: No, because there was no consideration to support the creditor's promise not to sue.
choices.B: No, because there was no consideration to support the debtor's promise to pay $1,000 on December 1.
choices.C: Yes, because a promise to allow a debtor to delay payment on a past debt is enforceable without consideration.
choices.D: Yes, because the debtor bargained for the creditor's forbearance.

questions.explanation:
Consideration problems that prevent contract formation
Gift No bargained-for exchange
Token consideration No inducement to bargain if performance entirely devoid of value
Sham consideration No legal detriment & no inducement to bargain if recited performance not intended to be completed
Preexisting duty / past consideration No legal detriment if performance already owed or completed
Illusory promise No legal detriment if apparent promise imposes no obligation

For any agreement to be enforceable, there must be consideration—ie, a bargained-for exchange of promises or performance. The promise to perform, or the performance of, a preexisting duty does not qualify as consideration. Under this preexisting duty rule, a debtor's promise to pay all or part of a liquidated debt (ie, one that is certain and undisputed) is not sufficient consideration to support a creditor's return promise.

Here, the debtor owed the creditor a liquidated and undisputed $1,000 debt that was due on March 1. When the debtor failed to pay, the creditor promised not to sue if the debtor promised to pay $1,000 by December 1. But there was no consideration to support the creditor's promise because the debtor had a preexisting duty to pay the $1,000 and promised to do nothing more than he was already obligated to do. Therefore, the parties' agreement was invalid for lack of consideration, and the court should not grant the debtor's motion to dismiss.

(Choices B & D) The creditor's promise not to sue (ie, forbearance) was sufficient consideration to support the debtor's promise to pay $1,000 on December 1. But there was no bargained-for consideration for the creditor's promise not to sue because the debtor promised to perform only a preexisting duty in return.

(Choice C) Under the preexisting duty rule, a promise to allow a debtor to delay payment on an undisputed debt is not enforceable without consideration.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the preexisting duty rule, a debtor's promise to pay a liquidated debt (ie, one that is certain and undisputed in amount) is not consideration for a creditor's return promise.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 74 cmt. c (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that payment of a liquidated and undisputed obligation is not consideration).
questions.zh-question:
一名债务人对一名债权人负有的1,000美元已清算且无争议的债务于3月1日到期。3月15日，当该债务仍未偿还时，债权人告知债务人，如果债务人承诺在12月1日或之前支付这1,000美元，那么债权人将不会为追讨该债务而提起诉讼。债务人口头同意了。4月1日，债权人起诉债务人，以追讨于3月1日到期的债务。债务人动议驳回债权人的起诉状。

法院是否应批准债务人的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为没有对价来支持债权人不起诉的承诺。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为没有对价来支持债务人于12月1日支付1,000美元的承诺。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为允许债务人延迟偿还已到期债务的承诺，在没有对价的情况下也具有强制执行力。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为债务人通过交易换取了债权人的暂缓追诉。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析

合同法 (Contracts) - 对价 (Consideration)
✅ 正确答案：选项 A 法院不应批准债务人的动议，因为债权人“不起诉”的承诺缺乏对价 (Consideration) 的支持。
⚖️ 核心法律规则
📜 已存义务规则 (Preexisting Duty Rule)

在普通法下，承诺履行一方已经有法律义务去履行的行为，不构成有效的对价。

如果债务是已清算且无争议的 (Liquidated and Undisputed)，债务人承诺支付该债务（即使是延迟支付），并不能作为债权人“不起诉”或“减少债务”承诺的有效对价。

🔍 案情深度解析
1
债务性质： 题目明确指出这笔1,000美元的债务是“已清算且无争议的”。这意味着债务人必须支付这笔钱，没有任何法律借口不付。
2
债权人的承诺： 债权人承诺“不起诉” (Promise not to sue/Forbearance)。这通常是一个有效的法律损害 (Legal Detriment)，可以作为对价。
3
债务人的承诺（关键点）： 债务人承诺在12月1日支付1,000美元。

问题在于：债务人本来就有义务支付这1,000美元。他并没有承诺做任何额外的、或法律上不需要做的事情（例如提前付款、支付利息、或用实物抵债）。
4
结论： 由于债务人只是承诺履行其已存义务，他没有提供任何新的对价。因此，债权人的回报承诺（不起诉）是无偿的赠与承诺，不具有法律约束力。债权人可以反悔并立即起诉。
❌ 为什么其他选项错误
选项 B 错误： 债务人的承诺确实没有对价支持（因为是已存义务），但这并不是法院拒绝动议的直接原因。关键点在于债权人的承诺是否有效。因为债权人的承诺无效，所以债务人不能以此为由要求驳回起诉。
选项 C 错误： 这是一个常见的误区。仅仅是“允许延迟付款”的承诺，如果没有额外的对价（如利息），在普通法下是不可执行的。
选项 D 错误： 虽然看起来像是“讨价还价” (Bargained for)，但因为债务人没有遭受任何新的法律损害 (Legal Detriment)，所以这种“交易”在法律上不构成有效的对价交换。
💡 MBE 抢分技巧
看到 "Liquidated and Undisputed Debt"（已清算且无争议债务）时，警报雷达要响起来！

如果题目问修改合同（如延期、少付钱结清），根据普通法，必须要有新的对价 (New Consideration)。

例外情况：
  • 提前付款 (Pay early)
  • 用不同方式付款 (e.g., stock instead of cash)
  • 存在真实的争议 (Honest dispute)
如果只是“晚点付全款”或“少付钱了事”，通常都是无效的修改。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A buyer sent a seller an offer to buy 50 tons of cotton of a specified quality. The offer contained no terms except those specifying the amount and quality of the cotton. The seller then sent an acknowledgment by fax. The acknowledgment repeated the terms of the buyer's offer and stated that shipment would occur within five days. Among 12 printed terms on the acknowledgment was a statement that any dispute about the cotton's quality would be submitted to arbitration. Neither the buyer nor the seller said anything further about arbitration.
The seller shipped the cotton, and it was accepted by the buyer. A dispute arose between the buyer and the seller as to the quality of the cotton, and the seller asserted that the dispute had to be submitted to arbitration. The buyer instead sued the seller in court.
In that suit, which of the following arguments best supports the seller's position that the buyer must submit the dispute to arbitration?

choices.A: Arbitration is a more efficient method of resolving disputes than resolving them in court.
choices.B: The provision for arbitration did not contradict any term in the buyer's offer.
choices.C: The provision for arbitration did not materially alter the parties' contract.
choices.D: The seller's acknowledgment containing a provision for arbitration constituted a counteroffer that was accepted by the buyer when it accepted delivery of the cotton.

questions.explanation:
Effect of new terms in reply to offer
Common law
(mirror-image)
  • Offer rejected
  • Reply treated as counteroffer
UCC
(battle of the forms) 		≥1 party is
nonmerchant
  • Offer accepted unless reply expressly required assent to new/revised terms
  • New/revised terms treated as proposed additions to contract
All parties are
merchants
  • Offer accepted unless reply expressly required assent to new/revised terms
  • New terms become part of contract unless:
    • offer expressly required assent to new terms
    • new terms materially alter contract or
    • offeror objects within reasonable time
  • Revised terms follow split authority & are either:
    • treated as new terms or
    • cancelled out under knockout rule
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

At common law, contract formation is governed by the mirror-image rule. But the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC)—which applies to contracts for the sale of goods (eg, cotton)—follows the battle-of-the-forms rule. Under this rule, an acceptance of an offer is effective even if it contains new terms. And if both parties (ie, offeror and offeree) are merchants, the new terms become part of the contract unless:

  • the offer expressly requires the offeror's assent to new terms
  • the offeror objects within a reasonable time or
  • the new terms materially alter the contract.

Here, both parties are likely merchants since the buyer offered to buy 50 tons of cotton. This offer was silent as to arbitration, so that provision in the seller's acknowledgement (acceptance) was a new term. The buyer's offer did not expressly require her assent to new terms, and she accepted the shipment without objecting to the new term. Therefore, the arbitration provision became part of the contract if it did not materially alter the contract, which supports the seller's position that the dispute must be resolved through arbitration.

(Choice A) To determine whether a contract dispute must be arbitrated, courts consider the intent of the parties as expressed in the contract—not whether arbitration is more efficient.

(Choice B) The standard for determining whether a new term becomes part of the contract is whether that term materially alters the contract—not whether it contradicts the offer.

(Choice D) Under the common law mirror-image rule, the seller's acknowledgment containing a new term would constitute a counteroffer. But since this transaction is governed by the UCC, the battle-of-the-forms rule applies.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the battle-of-the-forms rule, an acceptance is effective even if it contains new terms. If both parties are merchants, the new terms become part of the contract unless (1) the offer expressly required the offeror's assent to new terms, (2) the offeror objected within a reasonable time, or (3) the new terms materially alter the contract.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-207 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2019) (battle-of-the-forms rule).
questions.zh-question:
一位买方向一位卖方发出要约，欲购买50吨特定品质的棉花。该要约除了指明棉花的数量和品质外，不包含任何其他条款。卖方随后通过传真发出一份确认书。该确认书重述了买方要约中的条款，并声明将在五日内发货。在该确认书的12条印刷条款中，有一项声明规定，任何关于棉花品质的争议都将提交仲裁。买卖双方均未就仲裁事宜作进一步说明。

卖方发运了棉花，买方也接受了货物。后买卖双方就棉花的品质产生争议，卖方主张该争议必须提交仲裁。买方则选择在法院起诉卖方。

在该诉讼中，以下哪项论点最能支持卖方的立场，即买方必须将争议提交仲裁？

zh-choices.A: 仲裁是比法院诉讼更有效的争议解决方法。
zh-choices.B: 仲裁条款并未与买方要约中的任何条款相抵触。
zh-choices.C: 仲裁条款并未对双方的合同作出实质性变更。
zh-choices.D: 卖方包含仲裁条款的确认书构成了一项反要约，而买方在接受棉花交付时接受了该反要约。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Battle of the Forms
UCC § 2-207 Formation of Contracts

本题考察的是美国合同法中著名的“格式之战” (Battle of the Forms)，即当承诺 (Acceptance) 中包含与要约 (Offer) 不一致或额外的条款时，合同如何成立以及条款内容为何。

核心法律规则：UCC § 2-207 在涉及货物买卖 (Sale of Goods) 的合同中，适用《统一商法典》(UCC)。

与普通法 (Common Law) 的“镜像规则” (Mirror Image Rule) 不同，UCC 规定：
  • 包含新增条款的承诺仍然有效（构成 Acceptance，而非 Counteroffer）。
  • 如果双方都是商人 (Merchants)，新增条款自动成为合同的一部分，除非满足特定例外。
逻辑推演步骤

第一步：确定适用法律
交易标的是棉花 (Goods)，因此适用 UCC。

第二步：确定当事人身份
买卖 50 吨棉花属于商业交易，双方均被视为商人 (Merchants)。

第三步：应用 UCC § 2-207(2)
在商人之间，卖方确认书中的“仲裁条款”作为新增条款 (Additional Term)，将自动进入合同，除非：

  1. 要约明确限制承诺必须完全符合要约条款；
  2. 新增条款对合同构成了实质性变更 (Material Alteration)；或
  3. 要约人已提出异议或在合理时间内提出异议。

选项深度解析

✅ 选项 C (正确答案)
“仲裁条款并未对双方的合同作出实质性变更。”
卖方想要赢得仲裁，必须证明该条款已经成为了合同的一部分。根据上述规则，如果该条款不构成“实质性变更”，且买方未反对，它就自动进入合同。因此，这是卖方在法律上唯一可行的抗辩路径。
(注：虽然在实际判例中，许多法院认为仲裁条款属于实质性变更，但在本题的逻辑框架下，卖方必须主张它“不是”实质性变更才能胜诉。)

❌ 选项 A (错误)
“仲裁更有效率。”
这是政策性论点，而非法律依据。合同条款的效力取决于当事人的合意 (Mutual Assent) 和法律规则 (UCC)，而非哪种争议解决方式更优越。

❌ 选项 B (错误)
“未与要约条款相抵触。”
这混淆了标准。对于新增条款 (Additional Terms)，标准是“是否构成实质性变更”，而不是“是否抵触”。只有当条款相互冲突 (Different Terms) 时，才可能涉及“剔除规则” (Knockout Rule)，但这不适用于本案的纯新增条款。

❌ 选项 D (错误)
“构成反要约 (Counteroffer)。”
这是普通法 (Common Law) 的思维。在 UCC 下，除非卖方明确声明“接受以买方同意新条款为前提” (Expressly Conditional)，否则确认书就是承诺 (Acceptance)，合同已经成立。如果选 D，意味着合同成立的时间点推迟到了“收货”时，这不符合 UCC § 2-207(1) 的初衷。

考试技巧： 看到货物买卖 + 确认书中有新条款，立即定位 UCC § 2-207。如果是商人之间，记住关键词：Material Alteration (实质性变更)。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
On November 1, an accountant and a lawyer contracted for the sale of the law books the accountant had inherited from his father. The lawyer agreed to pay the purchase price of $10,000 when the accountant delivered the books on December 1.
On November 10, the lawyer received a signed letter from the accountant that stated: "I have decided to dispose of the bookshelves containing the law books you have already purchased. If you want the shelves, I will deliver them to you along with the books on December 1 at no additional cost to you. Let me know before November 15 whether you want them. I will not sell them to anyone else before then." On November 14, the lawyer faxed and the accountant received the following message: "I accept your offer of the shelves." The accountant was not a merchant with respect to either law books or bookshelves.
On November 12, the accountant told the lawyer that he had decided not to part with the shelves.
Will this communication operate as a legally effective revocation of his offer to deliver the shelves?

choices.A: No, because by delaying his acceptance until November 14, the lawyer detrimentally relied on the accountant's promise not to sell the shelves to anyone else in the meantime.
choices.B: No, because the accountant had given a signed assurance that the offer would be held open until November 15.
choices.C: Yes, because the accountant was not a merchant with respect to bookshelves.
choices.D: Yes, because the lawyer had a preexisting obligation to pay $10,000 for the law books.

questions.explanation:
Irrevocable offers
Type Description Consideration Duration
UCC Firm offer Merchant gives written & signed assurance that offer will remain open Not required Specified or reasonable time
Common law Option contract Offeror promises to keep offer open in exchange for consideration Required
Partial performance
(unilateral contracts)		 Offeror invites acceptance only by performance & offeree begins to perform Reasonable time for full performance
Promissory estoppel* Offeror could reasonably foresee reliance on offer & offeree reasonably relies to his/her detriment Not required Reasonable time
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.
*Also referred to as "detrimental reliance."

Under the UCC, an existing contract can be modified by agreement (ie, offer and acceptance) of the parties. An offer to modify a contract is generally revocable prior to acceptance. But such an offer is irrevocable if it is a firm offer—ie, a merchant's written and signed assurance that his/her offer will be kept open for a period of time.

Here, the accountant's letter offering to modify the sales contract was signed and assured the lawyer that the offer would be held open until November 15. Nevertheless, the accountant's offer was revocable since he is not a merchant with respect to bookshelves (Choice B). Therefore, the accountant effectively revoked the offer before it was accepted by telling the lawyer on November 12 that he had decided not to part with the shelves.

(Choice A) Under the doctrine of promissory estoppel, an otherwise revocable offer becomes irrevocable if (1) the offeror could reasonably foresee that the offeree would rely on the offer and (2) the offeree reasonably and detrimentally relied on that offer. But even if the lawyer reasonably relied on the accountant's offer, he suffered no detriment—eg, expenses to prepare for the shelves' delivery.

(Choice D) The fact that the lawyer had a preexisting obligation to pay $10,000 for the law books shows that there would have been no new consideration for the proposed modification. But consideration is not required to modify a sale-of-goods contract.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the UCC, an offer to modify a contract is generally revocable unless it is a firm offer—ie, a merchant's written and signed assurance that his/her offer will remain open for a period of time.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-205 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (firm offers).
questions.zh-question: 此沟通是否构成对其交付书架之要约的具有法律效力的撤销？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为通过将其接受延迟至11月14日，律师有害地信赖了会计师在此期间不将书架出售给他人的承诺。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为会计师已作出签名保证，该要约将保持开放至11月15日。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为就书架而言，该会计师并非商人。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为律师已有支付10,000美元购买法律书籍的既存义务。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts / Sales (UCC)

✅ 正确答案：C

是的，撤销有效。因为该会计师在书架交易中并非商人 (Merchant)，所以他的书面承诺不具有约束力。

⚖️ 核心考点：UCC 确定要约规则

本题适用 UCC (Uniform Commercial Code)，因为涉及货物（书架）的买卖/赠与。

一般规则： 要约人可以在受要约人接受之前的任何时间撤销要约，即使他承诺过会保留要约。

例外情况 (不可撤销)：

  1. 普通法 - 选择权合同 (Option Contract)： 必须有对价 (Consideration) 才能让要约不可撤销。
  2. UCC § 2-205 - 确定要约 (Firm Offer)： 无需对价，但必须满足以下所有条件：
    • 涉及货物买卖；
    • 有签署的书面文件 (Signed writing)；
    • 明确保证要约将保持开放；
    • 要约人必须是商人 (Merchant)。
🔍 案情深度分析

在本案中，会计师确实写了一封信（书面形式），并承诺在11月15日前不卖给别人（保证保持开放）。

但是，题目中有一个致命的关键事实：

"The accountant was not a merchant with respect to either law books or bookshelves."
（该会计师就法律书籍或书架而言，均非商人。）

由于会计师不是商人，UCC 的“确定要约”规则 (Firm Offer Rule) 不适用。因此，我们回到一般规则：没有对价的承诺是不可执行的。

会计师承诺保留要约仅仅是一个无偿的赠与承诺 (Gratuitous promise)，他在律师接受之前（11月14日之前）的11月12日通知律师撤销，该撤销是法律上有效的。

📊 概念对比表
特征 Option Contract
(普通法)		 Firm Offer
(UCC)
适用范围 服务、不动产等 货物 (Goods)
是否需要对价 需要 不需要
要约人身份 任何人 必须是商人
形式要求 无特定形式 必须书面签署
❌ 排除干扰项

选项 A 错误 (Promissory Estoppel)：
虽然“禁止反言” (Promissory Estoppel) 可以让要约不可撤销，但这要求受要约人有有害信赖 (Detrimental Reliance)。本案中，律师仅仅是“推迟接受”，并没有产生实际的经济损失或采取实质行动（如为此买了配套家具、拆了墙等）。仅是等待通常不足以构成有害信赖。

选项 B 错误 (Signed Assurance)：
这正是本题的陷阱。仅有“签署的保证”是不够的，UCC § 2-205 明确要求要约人必须是商人。非商人签署的保证没有法律约束力（除非有对价）。

选项 D 错误 (Preexisting Duty)：
虽然律师有支付书籍款项的义务，但这与书架的要约是否可撤销无关。此外，UCC 下修改合同不需要对价 (Consideration)，只需要善意 (Good faith)。但本题的关键在于要约被撤销了，而不是修改是否有效。

💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)：
在 MBE 合同法题目中，当看到“不可撤销要约” (Irrevocable Offer) 的考点时，首先判断是 UCC 还是 Common Law。如果是 UCC，立即寻找“Merchant”这个关键词。如果题目明确告诉你当事人“不是商人”，这通常就是解题的直接依据。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A car dealer owed a bank $10,000, due on June 1. The dealer subsequently sold a car to a buyer at a price of $10,000, payable at $1,000 per month beginning on June 1. The dealer then telephoned the bank to ask whether the bank would accept payments of $1,000 per month for 10 months beginning June 1, without interest, in payment of the dealer's debt to the bank. The bank agreed to that arrangement, and the dealer then asked the buyer to make his car payments directly to the bank. When the buyer tendered the first payment to the bank, the bank refused the payment, asserting that it would accept payment only from the dealer. On June 2, the bank demanded that the dealer pay the debt in full immediately. The dealer refused to pay, and the bank sued the dealer to recover the $10,000.
In this suit, which of the following arguments best supports the bank's claim for immediate payment?

choices.A: The agreement to extend the time for payment was not in writing.
choices.B: The dealer could not delegate its duty to pay to the buyer.
choices.C: The dealer gave no consideration for the agreement to extend the time of payment.
choices.D: The dealer's conduct was an attempted novation that the bank could reject.

questions.explanation:
Consideration problems that prevent contract formation
Gift No bargained-for exchange
Token consideration No inducement to bargain if performance entirely devoid of value
Sham consideration No legal detriment & no inducement to bargain if recited performance not intended to be completed
Preexisting duty / past consideration No legal detriment if performance already owed or completed
Illusory promise No legal detriment if apparent promise imposes no obligation

Contract modifications must generally be supported by new consideration—ie, each party must alter its duties in some way—unless the modification is fair and equitable in light of unanticipated circumstances. The promise to perform, or the performance of, a preexisting duty is insufficient for new consideration and will not discharge the parties' duties under the initial (ie, unmodified) contract.

Here, the car dealer owed the bank $10,000, due on June 1. When the dealer asked whether the bank would accept installment payments beginning on June 1, the bank agreed. But the reason for the dealer's request (ie, the car sale) is not a circumstance that renders consideration unnecessary since it was completely unrelated to the debt owed to the bank. And since the dealer had a preexisting duty to pay that debt, he gave no consideration for the agreement to extend the time of payment. Therefore, the bank has a claim for immediate payment.

(Choice A) A writing is not required to modify a contract unless the statute of frauds applies to the modified contract (not seen here).

(Choice B) Absent a contrary term, either party to a contract can delegate its duty of performance to a third party. However, this would not extinguish the party's liability for breach should the third party fail to perform.

(Choice D) A novation is a new contract that (1) substitutes a new party for one of the original parties, (2) discharges the original party's obligations, and (3) requires agreement by all the parties involved. But here, the bank never agreed to substitute the buyer or discharge the dealer's debt.

📌 Educational Objective

Modification of an existing contract requires new consideration unless the modification is fair and equitable due to unanticipated circumstances. A promise to perform a preexisting duty does not constitute new consideration.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 73 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that performance of a pre-existing legal duty is not consideration).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 89 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that modification of a contract without new consideration is binding if it is fair and equitable in view of unanticipated circumstances).
questions.zh-question:
一名汽车经销商欠银行10,000美元，应于6月1日到期。该经销商随后以10,000美元的价格将一辆汽车出售给一名买方，约定从6月1日起每月支付1,000美元。经销商接着致电银行，询问银行是否愿意接受从6月1日开始的为期10个月、每月1,000美元的无息付款，以清偿经销商对银行的债务。银行同意了该安排，经销商随后要求买方将其购车款直接支付给银行。当买方向银行提交第一笔付款时，银行拒绝了付款，声称其只接受来自经销商的付款。6月2日，银行要求经销商立即全额偿还债务。经销商拒绝支付，银行遂起诉经销商，要求追回10,000美元。

在本诉讼中，以下哪项论点最能支持银行要求立即付款的主张？

zh-choices.A: 延长付款期限的协议没有采用书面形式。
zh-choices.B: 经销商不能将其付款义务委托给买方。
zh-choices.C: 经销商未就延长付款期限的协议提供对价。
zh-choices.D: 经销商的行为是一次银行可以拒绝的试图进行的债务更新。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Consideration & Modification
核心问题：
银行同意接受分期付款来代替原本到期的一次性全额还款，这个“修改后的协议”是否有效？
正确答案解析 (选项 C)

本题考查的是普通法（Common Law）下的已存义务原则 (Pre-existing Duty Rule)。

⚖️ 法律规则 (The Rule) 在普通法下，修改合同需要新的对价 (New Consideration)。承诺履行一方已经有法律义务去履行的行为，不构成有效的对价。
1
原始义务：
经销商（Dealer）在6月1日有法律义务向银行支付 $10,000。
2
拟议的修改：
银行同意经销商分10个月偿还这 $10,000，且不收取利息。
3
对价分析：
经销商承诺做什么？他承诺分期支付 $10,000。但这笔钱是他本来就欠银行的。他没有承担任何新的法律上的损害（Legal Detriment），也没有给银行带来任何新的利益（实际上，分期付款对银行来说价值更低，因为损失了货币的时间价值）。

因此，银行“同意分期付款”的承诺是不可执行的 (Unenforceable)，因为经销商没有提供对价。银行可以随时反悔，要求立即全额付款。

为什么其他选项是错误的？
  • 选项 A (Statute of Frauds)：
    虽然某些合同修改需要书面形式，但本题的核心障碍不是形式问题，而是实质性的“缺乏对价”。即使有书面协议，没有对价的修改在普通法下依然无效。
  • 选项 B (Delegation)：
    经销商确实可以将付款义务委托（Delegate）给买方，但这并不能免除经销商自己的责任。银行拒绝买方付款并起诉经销商，关键在于银行有权要求立即全额还款，而不是谁来付钱的问题。
  • 选项 D (Novation)：
    债务更新 (Novation) 需要三方达成一致，明确免除原债务人的责任并由新债务人替代。本案中，银行从未同意免除经销商的债务，只是同意改变付款方式。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧

区分 Common Law 与 UCC：

  • 如果是货物买卖 (Sale of Goods)：修改合同不需要对价，只要是基于善意 (Good Faith)。(UCC § 2-209)
  • 如果是服务或债务 (Services/Debt)（如本题）：修改合同必须有新的对价。(Common Law)

做题时，首先判断合同类型，这往往决定了“修改是否有效”的判断标准。
